body.heading: The family trick
paragraphs: Here is a secret that makes reading much easier: words come in families. Every word in a family ends with the same chunk of sound. If you can read 'cat', you are one letter away from reading bat, hat, mat, rat and sat.
Learn the ending once — then just swap the first letter and read the whole family!

body.heading: The -at family
paragraphs: cat, bat, hat, mat, rat, sat, pat.
The cat sat on the mat in a hat. (Five family words in one silly sentence!)

body.heading: The -ig and -op families
paragraphs: The big pig can dig. The frog likes to hop on top.

body.heading: The -un and -et families
paragraphs: My pet got wet in the net — what a day!

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Pick a family and race: how many of its words can you read in twenty seconds?
2. Invent a nonsense family member — 'zat' in the -at family. It is not a real word, but you can still read it. That is the family trick working!

takeaway: Words that share an ending are a family — learn the ending (-at, -ig, -op) and swapping the first letter unlocks word after word.
materials: Just you and this page — no materials needed
supervision: A grown-up nearby is recommended for younger readers; the think-and-talk questions work well read aloud together.
safetyNotes: Reading only — no physical activity or materials are involved.
screenFreeExtension: Family shout game: one person calls an ending ('-op!'), everyone else shouts family words as fast as they can.
